OBJECTIVE: Recreate the original source video with two precise subject replacements: replace the original car with my orange Lamborghini from the supplied car reference template, and replace the original man with my supplied alien character reference. Preserve the original video's camera movement, timing, positioning, actions, choreography, environment, and background exactly as they appear in the source footage.
1. SOURCE VIDEO — MASTER REFERENCE
Use the uploaded original video as the master source for the entire sequence.
Preserve the original video frame by frame, including:
Exact camera angle, camera movement, framing, perspective, and lens characteristics.
Original scene duration, frame rate, timing, cuts, transitions, and shot sequence.
Exact background, architecture, environment, ground surfaces, lighting conditions, shadows, reflections, and atmospheric details.
Every original movement, gesture, interaction, and action performed by the man.
The car's original position, orientation, movement, speed, trajectory, and relationship to the camera and environment.
Original subject spacing, depth, scale, and spatial relationships.
Do not redesign, reinterpret, restage, or creatively alter the original scene. Treat the source video as a locked plate and replace only the designated subjects.
2. CAR REPLACEMENT — USE THE SUPPLIED CAR TEMPLATE
Completely replace the original car with the orange Lamborghini shown in my supplied car reference sheet.
The reference sheet defines the car's exact visual identity. Reproduce its appearance consistently throughout every frame.
Preserve these exact design characteristics:
Bright metallic orange bodywork with the same hue, finish, and reflections as the reference.
Low, aggressive Lamborghini supercar silhouette and precise body proportions.
Angular headlights with vivid blue-white illumination.
Black multi-spoke wheels, low-profile tires, dark windows, and black aerodynamic side intakes.
The distinctive bright green, ruffled lettuce-like aerodynamic trim running along the front splitter, side skirts, and rear diffuser.
Matching hood contours, windshield shape, roofline, door geometry, rear bodywork, and wheel placement.
All other visible design features shown in the car template.
Maintain the car's identity, proportions, materials, and recognizable details across every frame and camera angle. Do not simplify, redesign, recolor, or substitute any component.
POSITION AND MOVEMENT LOCK: The replacement car must occupy the exact same three-dimensional position, screen coordinates, orientation, perspective, and apparent scale as the original car in each corresponding frame. Match the original vehicle's movement, rotation, acceleration, braking, and interaction with the environment precisely.
If the original car is partially obscured, preserve the same occlusion. If it moves out of frame, the replacement must move out of frame at the same moment. Keep the wheels, bodywork, shadows, and reflections spatially consistent with the source footage.
Use the supplied car template as the appearance reference, not as a composition or scene reference.
3. CHARACTER REPLACEMENT — USE THE SUPPLIED ALIEN TEMPLATE
Completely replace the original man with the alien character shown in my supplied character reference sheet.
Reproduce the same character design throughout the entire video:
Pale blue-green skin.
Oversized, bulbous, wrinkled alien head with the same anatomical proportions as the reference.
Deep-set facial features, prominent nose, defined cheekbones, and narrow mouth.
Dark sunglasses matching the supplied reference.
Short grey-purple chin beard and facial hair, as depicted in the template.
Navy-blue zip-up hooded jacket with a grey inner hood.
Navy-and-white horizontally striped polo shirt.
Dark navy trousers with the same loose fit and gathered ankles.
White socks and dark navy athletic shoes matching the reference.
Use the character sheet's front, rear, profile, and three-quarter views to maintain accurate anatomy, clothing construction, colors, textures, and silhouette from every viewing angle.
CHARACTER IDENTITY LOCK: The alien must remain the same character in every frame. Do not change the head shape, facial proportions, sunglasses, beard, clothing, body proportions, or footwear. Do not introduce additional accessories or alter the outfit.
MOTION AND ACTION LOCK: Transfer the original man's exact performance to the alien character. Preserve all original body movements, walking patterns, gestures, arm and hand movements, head turns, posture changes, facial orientation, interactions, timing, and reactions.
The alien must perform the same actions in the same places and at the same moments as the original man. Match the original body position, center of mass, limb trajectories, foot placement, and contact points as closely as possible.
Adapt the character's anatomy to the original movement without changing the action itself. Maintain believable joints, natural cloth deformation, correct foot-to-ground contact, and consistent character scale. Keep the sunglasses, beard, clothing, and body geometry stable during movement.
Do not add new gestures, expressions, movements, or actions. Do not make the character independently animate or react differently from the original performer.
4. BACKGROUND AND ENVIRONMENT — ABSOLUTE LOCK
Preserve the original video's background exactly as recorded.
Do not regenerate, replace, extend, clean up, stylize, enhance, or modify the environment. Retain all original background objects, buildings, roads, furniture, vegetation, signs, people, and environmental details in their original positions, where present.
Preserve the original:
Lighting direction, intensity, and color temperature.
Environmental shadows, reflections, and ambient occlusion.
Camera exposure, color grading, contrast, and depth of field.
Weather, atmosphere, and background movement.
Camera shake, motion blur, focus changes, and perspective.
Only modify pixels necessary to replace the original car and the original man. Keep all unaffected pixels as close to the source footage as possible.
Where either subject passes in front of or behind another object, preserve the original depth ordering and occlusion. Reconstruct only the portions of the scene genuinely hidden by the subjects, matching the surrounding background seamlessly.
5. COMPOSITING AND REALISM
Integrate both replacement subjects into the existing footage rather than producing a newly staged scene.
Ensure:
Accurate perspective, scale, and spatial alignment.
Natural contact shadows and ground interaction.
Lighting and reflections consistent with the original environment.
Realistic wheel rotation and tire contact if the car moves.
Correct character-to-environment interactions.
Consistent motion blur matching the original camera and subject velocities.
Clean edges around the car, alien, clothing, wheels, and aerodynamic trim.
Stable textures and geometry across consecutive frames.
No flickering, morphing, warping, ghosting, or changes in subject identity.
No floating feet, sliding contact, distorted limbs, or implausible car deformation.
The bright orange paint and vivid green trim must remain visually recognizable while responding naturally to the source video's lighting. The alien's skin, clothing, sunglasses, and beard must retain their reference appearance under the same lighting conditions.
6. STRICT PRESERVATION RULES
The following elements must remain unchanged:
Original video background.
Original camera movement and composition.
Original video duration and edit sequence.
Original man's actions, timing, and motion.
Original car's trajectory, position, orientation, and timing.
Original interactions between the subjects and the environment.
The only intended visual changes are:
Original car → supplied orange Lamborghini design.
Original man → supplied alien character design.
Do not add text, logos, watermarks, visual effects, extra characters, extra vehicles, new scenery, or new camera shots. Do not alter the storyline or introduce creative interpretations.
7. OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS
Produce a photorealistic, temporally consistent video that follows the source footage as closely as possible.
Maintain the original resolution, aspect ratio, frame rate, duration, shot composition, and edit timing whenever supported by the video-generation workflow.
The final result should look as though the orange Lamborghini and the alien character were physically present when the original video was filmed.
FINAL PRIORITY: Source-video fidelity first, exact reference-design fidelity second, seamless photorealistic compositing third. Never sacrifice the original movement, timing, positioning, or background to improve the visual design.
Use the original video for motion and scene control, the Lamborghini template exclusively for car appearance, and the alien character sheet exclusively for character appearance.
